name: Rolls-Royce Power Systems AG
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Rolls-Royce Power Systems is the third-ranked data-center gen-set OEM and the fastest-growing of the four, with divisional revenue up 19 percent in FY2025 and 28 percent in the first half of 2026, an operating margin that went from 13.1 to 20.3 percent in eighteen months, and a book-to-bill of 1.8 times — a re-rating driven so heavily by data centers that Citigroup's August 2026 sum-of-the-parts makes Power Systems the largest single contributor to the value of the listed parent, ahead of Civil Aerospace. BACKGROUND. The Friedrichshafen-based division of Rolls-Royce Holdings plc (LSE: RR.), selling under the mtu brand, with Rolls-Royce Solutions GmbH as its largest subsidiary and MTU Friedrichshafen GmbH as the legal entity. More than 11,000 employees; the group is represented in 48 countries and supplies customers in more than 100. The division reports twice: inside the parent's segment accounts in sterling (FY2025 revenue £4,892m, underlying operating profit £852m, order intake £6.1bn) and on its own account in euros (FY2025 adjusted revenue €5.72bn, adjusted operating profit €995m, order intake €7.14bn) — the company itself cross-walks the two. Five strategic initiatives: energy generation, defence, marine, battery storage and service.
ecosystemRole: We assess Rolls-Royce Power Systems as the widest single-vendor product span in on-site data-center power that this corpus tracks: diesel gen-sets to 4,000 kVA, gas gen-sets and CHP, a diesel-rotary uninterruptible power supply in the mtu Kinetic PowerPack, a grid-scale battery line in the mtu EnergyPack, a microgrid controller in mtu EnergetIQ, and, since February 2026, prefabricated 10, 20 and 30 MW gas power-plant modules aimed explicitly at bridge power. Its own commercial framing is the same: the VP of powergen sales for the Americas states that this makes it "the only major and experienced player offering diesel and gas gensets plus dynamic UPS systems." Basis: the mtu data-center landing page, the Kinetic PowerPack product data, the EnergyPack QS/QL/QG datasheets and the MEPP launch. Collection gap: the breadth is verifiable and the customer list is not — no hyperscaler, colocation landlord or neocloud in this corpus is named as a gen-set customer in any first-party or third-party source, and the company's own H1 2026 results refer only to unnamed "framework agreements with data centre customers."

productsAndServices.name: mtu Series 4000 diesel generator sets — 1,600 to 4,000 kVA (50 Hz) / 1,125 to 3,250 kWe (60 Hz)
productsAndServices.description: The flagship data-center line. Per the product brochure the family is "available in six different power ratings, including standby, prime and continuous" across 12V, 16V and 20V engines on a 90-degree V with a 170/210 mm bore and stroke, 4.77 litres per cylinder — 57.2 L on the 12V, 76.3 L on the 16V and 95.4 L on the 20V — at a 16.4:1 compression ratio with common rail to 1,800 bar. The 50 Hz ladder runs 12V4000 DS1650 through 20V4000 DS4000; the 60 Hz ladder runs DS1250 to DS3250, the highest published 60 Hz node at 3,250 kWe standby.
highlights: Certified "for ISO 8528, CE/IEC, NFPA 110 and German Grid Code (VDE-AR-4110)" — and "the first generator set in its performance class to be certified by the VDE-AR-4110 according to code MSR2008"

Rated across five duties, of which Data center continuous power (3F) carries a 100 percent load factor, unlimited annual hours, 10 percent overload and Uptime Institute Tier III and Tier IV compliance

"In case of an emergency, our mtu Series 4000 generator sets will provide their full electrical power within a few seconds"; the hardest published number is 15 seconds to full electrical output, from the EdgeConneX Amsterdam reference
Overhaul interval up to 48,000 hours; voltages from 380 V to 11,000 V; radiator packages for 40 and 50 degrees C ambient; circuit breakers to 5,000 A
"Fuels according to EN15940 are approved for all Series 4000 system configurations and emission calibrations" — HVO across the whole range, not a variant
More than 50,000 units sold and more than 180 million operating hours since 1996
productsAndServices.positioning: Ranked third in data-center generators for 2025 by MarketsandMarkets behind Caterpillar and Cummins, credited with traction "in high-density AI and hyperscale environments." A lead-time survey by Terrapin Consulting Group states that "Caterpillar and MTU often have the shortest lead times for larger hyperscale tier units" — which is the company's own claimed differentiator: it says it competes "on power density, speed of back-up and service."
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct plus a distributor network of more than 420 sales and service partners, and system integrators — AVK holds exclusivity for mtu emergency-power gen-sets in the UK and Ireland to 2031
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centers and mission-critical, healthcare, airports, industrial plants, decentralised power stations, microgrids
productsAndServices.roadmap: "Our next generation Series 4000 engine, to be released in 2028, which targets the data centre market with a significantly improved power density" — reported at more than 20 percent additional power output, having completed 500 hours of test-bench running by FY2025 results

productsAndServices.name: mtu Series 2000 and Series 1600 diesel generator sets — 590 to 1,270 kVA
productsAndServices.description: The mid and lower nodes. Series 2000 covers 770 to 1,270 kVA at 50 Hz and 680 to 1,250 kWe at 60 Hz; Series 1600, upgraded for the 50 Hz market in February 2025, covers 590 to 1,000 kVA on a 12V1600 Gx1 engine delivering up to 996 kWm — 40 percent more power than its predecessor.
highlights: Series 2000 accepts "extremely high load steps without significant frequency and voltage deviations, overachieving ISO 8528-5 performance class G2 and G3", with "100% block load acceptance according to NFPA 110 requirements"
Series 2000 was "the first genset in its performance class to be certified according to grid code VDE-AR-N 4110"
Series 1600 is compliant with "ISO 8528 DCP (Data Center Power)" and the Uptime Institute Tier III and Tier IV topology levels, with load factors up to 100 percent
"All mtu Series 1600 generator sets are approved for synthetic fuels such as hydrogenated/hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO)"
Series 2000 engine assembly was relocated to the Kluftern plant, opened in 2023 at roughly 30 million euros with 110 staff, to free Friedrichshafen Plant 2 for Series 4000
productsAndServices.positioning: The edge and smaller-hall range, and the node band where Cummins and Rehlko are described as most competitive
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Edge and enterprise data centers, healthcare, commercial standby

productsAndServices.name: mtu Series 4000 gas generator sets and CHP — 776 to 2,547 kWe
productsAndServices.description: The lean-burn gas line, offered as combined heat and power and combined heat, power and cooling. The 60 Hz natural-gas table runs the 8V4000 GS at 997 kWel through the 20V4000 GS at 2,520 kWel, all on the L64FNER engine at 43.6 to 43.9 percent electrical efficiency and 88.6 to 89.0 percent total efficiency with a methane number requirement of 72 or better. Time before overhaul is 84,000 hours.
highlights: Existing units reach full load in 120 seconds; the new 20V4000 L64 for 60 Hz delivers 2.8 MW in 45 seconds from 2026, a 10 percent output increase on the previous version and a gearbox-free design

The 45-second figure is the company's answer to the load-acceptance objection that normally disqualifies gas from data-center duty — against Caterpillar's roughly seven seconds on the G3516 and Jenbacher's two minutes on the J920
H2-ready certificate from TUV Sud for the current Series 4000 FNER and FV gas engines; 100 percent hydrogen CHP plants operational since summer 2025

Deployed in a 10 MW UK plant at Worksop with carbon-dioxide recovery of up to 30,000 tonnes a year, and in 24 containerised 10 MW units totalling 60 MW for the Dutch grid operator Stedin to relieve grid bottlenecks from 2026 to 2036
productsAndServices.positioning: The prime-power line, historically less than 10 percent of the division's power-generation business and targeted at 15 to 20 percent by 2030
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data-center bridge and prime power, cogeneration, grid support, industrial

productsAndServices.name: mtu Kinetic PowerPack — diesel rotary uninterruptible power supply, 480 to 3,000 kVA
productsAndServices.description: A battery-free dynamic UPS: an mtu diesel engine, a four-pole synchronous machine, a kinetic energy accumulator and an electromagnetic clutch on a single base frame with redundant start, manufactured in Liege, Belgium. Sold as the KP5 and KP7 from 480 kVA / 400 kW to 2,750 kVA / 2,640 kW, with solution-guide tables reaching 3,000 kVA / 2,400 kW at 60 Hz. It is the reason the division can claim diesel, gas and UPS from one supplier.
highlights: "Reducing its footprint to 40% of an equivalently rated static UPS system - making it the smallest in the market"
20-plus years' design life and a 10-year bearing life, with vibration reduced by more than 97 percent
Conditions supply to within plus or minus 0.4 Hz and plus or minus 10 percent, and delivers 17 times nominal current into a short circuit — a fault-current contribution a static UPS cannot match
Published in both Standby power (3D) and Data center continuous power (3F) ratings at 50 and 60 Hz
Emissions options include US EPA stationary emergency Tier 2 (40 CFR 60), US Nonroad Tier 2 and Tier 3, EU Nonroad Stage II and NEA Singapore
Two 1,500 kW units supplied to NOVVA Data Centers in Colorado Springs in June 2024
productsAndServices.positioning: The rotary UPS is a small and specialised segment where Piller is the corpus's other covered vendor; Rolls-Royce is unusual in selling it alongside the engines rather than as a standalone franchise.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Colocation and hyperscale data centers, semiconductor fabs, broadcast

productsAndServices.name: mtu EnergyPack — battery energy storage, cabinet to grid scale
productsAndServices.description: Three current products. The QS outdoor cabinet runs to 625 kWh and 400 kVA on NMC cells; the QL, a complete system inside a 40-foot high-cube container, runs to 2,084 kWh and 2,000 kVA on NCM with 50 kA short-circuit capability; the QG is the grid-scale line, scaling from base units of 3 to 36 MWh and 3 to 9 MVA on "latest LFP cell chemistry with zero degradation as an option," delivered at 10 to 33 kV as an all-in-one solution with medium and high-voltage integration. All three are controlled by mtu EnergetIQ.
highlights: QS and QL both offer "grid-supporting & grid-forming mode" with controlled switching between them, plus black start — the capability that lets a battery hold an islanded site while engines start

QG publishes a system response time of about 150 ms with "grid-forming capability, virtual inertia, and black start functionality", 1 to 4 hour discharge (0.25 to 1 C), and cells claimed to give "zero degradation for up to five years and up to 15,000+ cycle lifetime"
Extended warranties to 15 years, with long-term service agreements carrying performance and availability guarantees
More than 150 projects in 45 countries and more than 635 MWh installed; the business reached breakeven in FY2025

Largest order to date: 582 MWh / 291 MW for Ignitis Group across three Lithuanian sites from 2027. Also 490 MWh for Sunly in Latvia and 43 MW / 86 MWh for Voltaria in Falkirk, Scotland on CATL cells with a 15-year service agreement

The deployments are grid and utility scale: no data-center EnergyPack installation was found in any source. The data-center storage product is the Kinetic PowerPack, which is a rotary UPS, not a battery
productsAndServices.positioning: Positioned as "the leading supplier of battery storage in the Baltic states" with more than 1,500 MWh contracted there; front-of-meter grid firming rather than behind-the-meter data-center storage
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC and turnkey, including planning, permitting support, construction, commissioning and long-term service
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utilities, IPPs, renewables firming, grid stability
productsAndServices.roadmap: Guidance is for double-digit original-equipment revenue growth in BESS to the mid-term

productsAndServices.name: mtu EnergetIQ — microgrid and BESS control
productsAndServices.description: Two products: the EnergetIQ BESS Controller for battery control, protection and analytics, and the EnergetIQ Manager, described as a "SCADA system, switch gear- and power plant controller, application manager, microgrid controller." The Manager carries twelve modules spanning data management, a group controller, a system optimizer using model-predictive control with AI load prediction and weather and price forecasts, and asset controllers for fuel cells, electrolyzers, BESS, renewables, gen-sets and CHP, dynamic UPS, fuel storage and switchgear.
highlights: Operates "on-grid, off-grid, on- & off-grid" with controller, ethernet and I/O redundancy options
Speaks OPC-UA, Modbus TCP and RTU, Profibus DP, ProfiNet, DNP3, IEC 60870-5-101/103/104 and IEC 61850 — the protocol list is the measure of how many third-party seams it has to cross
"Certified according to IEC 62443-4-1 ML2 and aligned with ISO 27001 and NIST2 requirements"
Names switchgear as "the electrical backbone" of the controlled plant
productsAndServices.positioning: The layer that makes a diesel, gas, battery and UPS portfolio behave as one plant — and the differentiation a single-source buyer is actually purchasing
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with EnergyPack and MEPP scopes, and sold into microgrid projects
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Microgrids, islanded campuses, hybrid data-center plants

productsAndServices.name: Modular Engine Power Plants (MEPP) — 5 MW to 100 MW and beyond
productsAndServices.description: Launched February 2026: prefabricated gas power-plant modules in 10 MW and 20 MW "Power Squad" and 30 MW "Power Tower" configurations, scaling from 5 MW to several hundred megawatts, with a stated lead time of 12 to 18 months from order placement. Hydrogen-ready and capable on biomethane and biogas.
highlights: Applications named at launch include grid backup, renewables firming, data centres and bridge power "until grid or alternative power source connection" — the first time the division has productised the bridge-power case
Reference plants cited: Ahlen Germany 12 MW, Chatterley Whitfield UK 20 MW, Pekanbaru Indonesia 33 MW, Myingyan Myanmar 150 MW, Atacama Chile 294 MW
Senior VP Strategy Michael Stipa at launch: "True resilience comes from decentralization, not centralization"

Business Unit president Tobias Ostermaier framed it as implementing the German Government's Power Plant Strategy "quickly and economically" — a policy-driven demand channel alongside the data-center one
productsAndServices.positioning: The answer to a grid-connection queue measured in years; competes with Wartsila, INNIO/Jenbacher and Caterpillar's gas fleets for bridge duty
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centers awaiting grid connection, grid operators, renewables firming

productsAndServices.name: Gendrive engines sold to gen-set packagers
productsAndServices.description: Series 4000 Gx4 engines sold bare to third-party gen-set builders with published 3D, 3E and 3F ratings. At 1,500 rpm the range runs from the 12V G74F at 1,575 kW to the 20V4000 G94LF at 3,308 kW; at 1,800 rpm from the 12V G74S at 1,736 kW to the 20V4000 G94S at 3,490 kW.
highlights: The Gendrive spec sheet carries the division's cleanest rating-definition table, distinguishing standby (3D), prime for stationary emergency (3E) and data center continuous power (3F) by load factor, annual hours and overload capability
Emission optimisations offered include US EPA Nonroad Tier 2 stationary (40 CFR 60), US EPA Nonroad Tier 2 (40 CFR 89), NEA Singapore for ORDE and China NRMM Stage III
Selling engines to packagers puts mtu inside competitors' gen-sets, the mirror image of Cummins' alternator business
productsAndServices.positioning: A merchant engine franchise beneath the branded gen-set business

productsAndServices.name: Service and aftermarket — mtu ValueCare Agreements
productsAndServices.description: Maintenance, repair and overhaul, annual checks, technical documentation, training, commissioning, genuine parts, consumables and remanufactured products, delivered through more than 350 service partners. Services revenue was £1,459m in FY2025, up 12 percent, and 70 percent of divisional revenue in the first half of 2026.
highlights: Services were 70 percent of H1 2026 divisional revenue and grew 17 percent, against original equipment at 30 percent growing 33 percent
The installed base the service business runs against is stated as more than 85,000 mtu emergency power systems and more than 17 GW of installed capacity with mtu engines
The AVK framework is an integrator relationship rather than a service one: more than 600 mtu gen-sets supplied to AVK over the past decade
productsAndServices.positioning: The margin ballast under a cyclical equipment business, and the reason divisional margin held up through the transition

productsAndServices.name: Governmental, marine and rail
productsAndServices.description: The non-power-generation majority of the division's original-equipment mix. Governmental covers the mtu Series 199 for land vehicles and PowerPacks, with a 2025 order for more than 300 Leopard 2 engines and, in the first half of 2026, 350 Series 199 engines for Boxer and roughly 200 compact PowerPacks for Puma. Marine covers Series 2000, 4000 and 8000 propulsion and gen-sets, with methanol-ready certification in August 2026. Rail covers PowerPacks and the Series 4000 R03.
highlights: Governmental original-equipment revenue is guided to grow about 20 percent a year to 2030, marine at 5 to 7 percent

Recorded here because the division's data-center growth is riding on a business whose defence order book is expanding at a similar rate — capacity is being competed for internally as well as externally
productsAndServices.positioning: Context for the capacity constraint rather than an ecosystem capability

recentDevelopments.headline: Methanol-ready certification achieved for mtu marine engines, and the portfolio of variable-speed marine gen-sets expanded
recentDevelopments.read: Marine rather than data-center news, but the variable-speed architecture is the same one that decouples engine speed from output frequency in a hybrid plant.

recentDevelopments.headline: 33 mtu engines ordered for the modernisation of the Korean freight locomotive fleet
recentDevelopments.read: Rail volume competing for the same Friedrichshafen assembly capacity the data-center book needs.

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026: Power Systems revenue £2,604m (+28%), underlying operating profit £528m (+72%), margin 20.3% (+5.3 points), order intake £4.6bn with a book-to-bill of 1.8x; power generation was 58% of original-equipment revenue and grew 41%, with power-generation order intake up 55%
recentDevelopments.read: The strongest half the division has reported, and the point at which management raised the power-generation growth target from 20 to 25 percent a year to 2030.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Rolls-Royce Power Systems has been re-rated by data centers more completely than any other gen-set OEM in this corpus, and that the parent's equity story now depends on it. Basis: divisional margin moved from 13.1 percent in FY2024 to 17.4 percent in FY2025 to 20.3 percent in H1 2026, against a mid-term target that was itself raised from 14-16 to 18-20 percent; order intake reached £6.1bn in FY2025 and £4.6bn in the first half of 2026 alone, a book-to-bill of 1.8 times; and Citigroup's note of 2026-08-17 makes Power Systems the largest single contributor to its sum-of-the-parts at 504 pence against Civil Aerospace's 353 pence, explicitly "boosted by surging data centre demand." Citi forecasts a long-term divisional margin of 23.5 percent, above the company's own 18-20 percent target.

(High confidence) We assess that the division's differentiation is breadth of the on-site power stack, not any single product's superiority. Basis: it is the only vendor in this corpus selling diesel gen-sets, gas gen-sets, a rotary UPS, a grid-scale battery, a microgrid controller and prefabricated power-plant modules under one brand, and its own VP of powergen sales for the Americas states the diesel-plus-gas-plus-dynamic-UPS combination makes it "the only major and experienced player" doing so. The corollary is that the breadth is only worth what the integration is worth, which is why mtu EnergetIQ — a controller speaking eleven industrial protocols and certified to IEC 62443-4-1 — is the piece to examine, not the engines.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the battery business is not a data-center business and should not be counted as one. Basis: every EnergyPack deployment located is grid or utility scale — 582 MWh for Ignitis in Lithuania, 490 MWh for Sunly in Latvia, 43 MW for Voltaria in Scotland, systems for Eleqtis in the Netherlands — and the company's own positioning claim is that it is "the leading supplier of battery storage in the Baltic states." No data-centre EnergyPack installation was found in first-party or third-party sources. The division's data-center storage product is the Kinetic PowerPack, a diesel rotary UPS, which is a different machine solving a different problem. Conflating the two overstates the AIDC franchise.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the division is strong in standby and weak in the gigawatt prime-power awards that are currently being written, and that the fast-start gas engine is the response. Basis: POWER Magazine's March 2026 survey of reciprocating-engine data-center power tabulates named gigawatt-scale wins for Caterpillar (2 GW at Monarch, 4 GW with Joule), INNIO/Jenbacher (2.3 GW with VoltaGrid) and Wartsila (429 MW plus a 790 MW Texas order), and lists Rolls-Royce on product attributes and installed base with no named deal. The CEO's own figure is that prime power is "less than 10%" of the power-generation business today, targeted at 15-20 percent by 2030. The 45-second, 2.8 MW 20V4000 L64 and the MEPP modular plants are both dated 2026 and both aimed squarely at that gap.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that supply, not demand, is the binding constraint, and that the division is contracting capacity rather than price. Basis: the AVK agreement is explicitly a guarantee of production slots in exchange for committed order volumes; the CEO states orders are being taken for 2028 and framework agreements run to 2030 with penalties; Mankato is stated to more than double Series 4000 gen-set output; Aiken adds engine machining; Friedrichshafen Plant 3 adds Series 4000 assembly from 2028. A third party puts mtu among the shortest lead times for large hyperscale units, which if true is a commercial weapon in a market where the industry runs 50 to 110 weeks.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the ownership question that hung over this division for a decade is settled in the opposite direction from where it started. Basis: Bloomberg reported in November 2023 that Rolls-Royce would keep a Power Systems business "that some analysts had seen as a disposal candidate"; the 2023 Capital Markets Day placed it in the invest-and-grow rather than the exit bucket; the only perimeter change since was the disposal of the sub-480 kW engine business to DEUTZ, completed August 2024. No 2025 or 2026 source reports an active sale or strategic review. A division that is now the parent's largest sum-of-the-parts contributor is not a disposal candidate.

(Low confidence) We assess that customer concentration is the material unpriced risk, and that it cannot be sized from public information. Basis: trade press attributes to Rolls-Royce a figure of more than 80 percent of Power Systems power-generation revenue coming from data centres, which sits alongside the company's own H1 2026 disclosure that power generation is 58 percent of divisional original-equipment revenue — different denominators, and the 80 percent figure does not appear in the transcript or the results release. Collection gap: no hyperscaler, colocation landlord or neocloud is named as a customer in any source, the framework agreements are unnamed, and no named-broker note warning specifically on this concentration was found. The penalties clause the CEO describes is the only stated mitigation, and its terms are not public.

relationships.note: Co-authored a position paper with Microsoft on hydrotreated vegetable oil for backup power in Singapore's data-centre sector.
relationships.context:
Published 2025-08-28, the paper argues for HVO in data-centre standby fleets against the Singapore Green Data Centre Roadmap, which allocates about 300 MW of near-term capacity with 200 MW reserved for operators using green energy options. Microsoft's Cloud ESG Planning Director for Asia Pacific is quoted in the release alongside Rolls-Royce's President Global Markets.

This is policy advocacy, not an equipment order. No source in this research names Microsoft, or any other hyperscaler, as a purchaser of mtu gen-sets, and Rolls-Royce's own H1 2026 results refer only to unnamed "framework agreements with data centre customers." The link is recorded at the strength the source supports and no further.

relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets ranks the 2025 data-center generator field Caterpillar, Cummins, Rolls-Royce, Rehlko, Mitsubishi. The competition is sharpest in prime power: POWER Magazine's March 2026 survey lists Caterpillar with 2 GW at the Monarch Compute Campus and up to 4 GW with Joule Capital Partners, against no named gigawatt-scale award for mtu, and quotes Caterpillar's G3516 ramping "zero to full load in approximately seven seconds" against mtu's 45 seconds on the new fast-start gas set. In standby the ordering is closer, and a lead-time survey places Caterpillar and mtu together as having the shortest lead times for large hyperscale units.

Terrapin Consulting Group's 2026 lead-time survey splits the two by node band: "Caterpillar and MTU often have the shortest lead times for larger hyperscale tier units" while "Cummins and Kohler tend to be competitive at the 1,000-2,000 kW range." Both are expanding US capacity concurrently — Cummins committing $450M for 20 GW of high-horsepower output, Rolls-Royce doubling Series 4000 gen-set assembly at Mankato and adding engine machining at Aiken.

The two are structurally similar in a way the American vendors are not: Rehlko's G-Drive engines for the whole 700-4000 kW range are built by Liebherr at Colmar in France and its power-control business manufactures at Cholet, while Rolls-Royce assembles at Friedrichshafen and Kluftern — both therefore run a Europe-to-US supply chain into the American data-center market. Both are also expanding capacity into the same demand: Rehlko states a plan to lift capacity by more than 400 percent through the decade, Rolls-Royce to more than double Series 4000 output at Mankato.

relationships.context: POWER Magazine's March 2026 survey of engine power plants for data centers tabulates Wartsila with 24 Wartsila 50SG units totalling 429 MW, a 123 MW Odessa Texas project and 75 MW in Kentucky, alongside separate 790 MW Texas and Liberty Energy orders in April and June 2026; mtu appears in the same table on technology and installed base, with no named deal. policyExposure.regime: US EPA stationary emissions tiers (40 CFR 60)
policyExposure.exposure: The 60 Hz data-center catalogue is published across classes: EPA Tier 2 certified sheets, frequently annotated with South Coast Air Quality Management District compliance (for example the 20V4000 DS3250 at 3,250 kWe); an EPA Tier 4 certified 20V4000 DS3000 at 3,000 kWe; and fuel-consumption-optimised variants that carry no emissions certification. The Kinetic PowerPack adds US EPA stationary emergency Tier 2 (40 CFR 60), US Nonroad Tier 2 (40 CFR 89) and US Nonroad Tier 3. Gendrive engines add NEA Singapore for ORDE and China NRMM Stage III (GB20981-2014).

Certification to the German grid code is a published product feature rather than a compliance footnote. The Series 4000 is stated to be "the first generator set in its performance class to be certified by the VDE-AR-4110 according to code MSR2008", and the Series 2000 "the first genset in its performance class to be certified according to grid code VDE-AR-N 4110." Sets are described as "suitable for grid parallel operation for monthly test runs or to gain additional revenues through grid services such as frequency control reserve." The 50 Hz DS4000 sheet carries a unit certificate to VDE-AR-N 4110.
policyExposure.mitigation: Grid-code certification is what converts an emergency-only asset into one that can earn from frequency services, and the company markets it that way alongside German Renewable Energy Act levy and formaldehyde-bonus support for customers.

policyExposure.exposure: The rating structure is mapped explicitly to certification outcomes: standby (3D), prime for stationary emergency (3E), prime (3B) and grid stability (3G) map to Uptime Tier I and II, while data center continuous power (3F) maps to Tier III and Tier IV. The company also publishes a comparison showing where its own definitions are more generous than ISO 8528-1 — a 3D load factor of 85 percent against ISO's 70 percent for emergency standby power, and 500 annual hours against ISO's 200.

Gen-set sheets state that the unit "accepts rated load in one step per NFPA 110"; battery site clearances are specified "according to NFPA 855" in the EnergyPack QG datasheet, alongside UN38.3, UL1973, IEC 62619, UL9540A, IEC 62477, IEC 62933-5-2 and IEC 61000-6-2/6-4. Seismic certification to the 2021 IBC and HCAI pre-approval, UL 2200 and CSA C22.2 are offered as options on the 60 Hz gen-sets.

"Fuels according to EN15940 are approved for all Series 4000 system configurations and emission calibrations", and all Series 1600 gen-sets are approved for HVO. The company publishes reductions of up to 90 percent in lifecycle carbon dioxide, about 80 percent in particulate matter and up to 8 percent in nitrogen oxides on HVO, and states that "no engine hard- or software adaptions" are necessary and that standard warranty conditions apply. In December 2025 it published the first Environmental Product Declarations for data-centre emergency gen-sets, through Environdec with Sphera, to ISO 14025 and EN 50693.
policyExposure.mitigation: A published EPD gives a data-centre customer the cradle-to-grave figure its own carbon disclosure requires — a procurement credential rather than an emissions one.

policyExposure.exposure: The EnergetIQ and EnergyPack QG control layer is "certified according to IEC 62443-4-1 ML2 and aligned with ISO 27001 and NIST2 requirements", and the modular power-plant flyer lists "certified cybersecurity" as a feature. This matters because the controller speaks eleven industrial protocols and sits between the utility interface and the plant.

At the launch of the Modular Engine Power Plants, Business Unit president Tobias Ostermaier framed the product as implementing the German Government's Power Plant Strategy "quickly and economically." This is a policy-created demand channel for the same gas modules being sold into data-center bridge power, and it competes for the same manufacturing slots.

Collection gap rather than an assessed exposure. Rolls-Royce discloses tariffs only at group level — the CEO refers to having "navigated challenges from supply chain to tariffs" and the going-concern assessment cites "the uncertainty introduced by tariffs" — with no quantified Power Systems figure. The division's structural exposure is real and undisclosed: Series 4000 engines are machined in Germany and assembled at Mankato, Minnesota, and the Aiken, South Carolina investment is explicitly described as onshoring machining that currently happens in Germany.

Recorded as a negative finding. No mtu power-generation specification sheet reviewed references EU Stage V. The European emissions level that does appear on 50 Hz power-generation gear is EU Nonroad Stage II (97/68/EC), on the Kinetic PowerPack sheets. Stage V under Regulation (EU) 2016/1628 governs non-road mobile machinery rather than stationary emergency gen-sets, which are regulated nationally in the EU — which is consistent with what the company publishes, but the absence is stated here because a buyer comparing a European and an American vendor will expect to see it.

periods.commentary: Reported 2026-02-26. Power Systems was the single largest source of the group's beat: 18.8 percent ahead of consensus on divisional operating profit against 5.7 percent at group level. Rolls-Royce Power Systems AG separately reported adjusted revenue of EUR 5.72bn (+19%), adjusted operating profit of EUR 995m and a 17.4 percent return on sales, with order intake of EUR 7.14bn (+21%) including a December order for 300 Leopard tank engines. The divisional mid-term margin target was raised to 18-20 percent from 14-16 percent. Two consumer trackers disagree on whether the group EPS line beat: Investing.com scores it +17.5 percent and TipRanks in line; both use half-year-shaped splits that do not reconcile to the reported full-year figures, so the company-compiled consensus is the figure carried here.

periods.commentary: Reported 2026-07-30. The company-compiled consensus is annual only, so there is no divisional half-year benchmark — the group figures below are measured against S&P Global Visible Alpha estimates cited by Alliance News, and no consensus of any kind was found for Power Systems at the half. Guidance was raised above the standing analyst consensus: the July 2026 company-compiled consensus had FY2026 group operating profit at £4,198m and Power Systems at £1,080m on £5,763m of revenue, and management guided to £4.7-4.9bn of group operating profit and £3.8-4.0bn of free cash flow. The power-generation original-equipment growth target was raised from 20 to 25 percent a year to 2030.

metrics.name: Power Systems revenue
metrics.result: No divisional half-year consensus exists from any source. Original equipment was £1,824m (+33%) and services £780m (+17%).

metrics.name: Power Systems underlying operating profit
metrics.result: The highest divisional margin on record and above the raised 18-20 percent mid-term target.

metrics.name: Power Systems order intake
metrics.result: Original-equipment order coverage is about 100 percent for 2026 and more than 50 percent for 2027.

metrics.name: Power Systems data-centre disclosure
metrics.actual: Power generation was 58% of original-equipment revenue and grew 41%; power generation order intake rose 55%; the CFO separately told CNBC that data-centre power orders rose more than 50%
metrics.result: Trade press attributes to Rolls-Royce a figure of more than 80 percent of power-generation revenue coming from data centres; that figure does not appear in the results release or the transcript and is carried as trade-press attribution only.
